title: I've been vibe coding Deep Fried, a dungeon-diving roguelite inspired by Delicious in Dungeon!
author: rychder
selftext:
This is a fun side project for me and has been helping me learn about the game devlopment pipeline. Claude is doing the majority of the heavy lifting with code and execution, while Gemini is contributing the character and food artwork!

It's free, plays in your browser, and is optimized for mobile and desktop: [https://ryderlink.itch.io/deep-fried](https://ryderlink.itch.io/deep-fried)

The idea: you dive into a living dungeon called the Gullet, fight monsters, butcher them into ingredients, and cook meals at camp between floors. Meals are your only source of mana and health regen so the quality of the ingredients you collect is essential. You can head home after any floor to bank your haul, but if you die, the dungeon takes half of your inventory from your current run.

This is an ever-evolving work in progress so I'm welcoming any and all feedback.

comments.author: thetinytrex
comments.body: Dungeon meshi is one of my favorite anime. Looks cool. I would just work on the UI and have the artwork consistent with the pixel art. The pixel art game itself looks great but as soon as I see the UI, it really ruins the look of the game.

replies.author: rychder
replies.body: This view surprises me! I actually made a conscious choice to move away from pixel style artwork for the food and the character art to try to get closer to the feel of Dungeon Meshi, the artwork of their feasts is one of my favorite parts of the anime. I get what you’re saying though, the conflicting art styles can be jarring.

replies.author: thetinytrex
replies.body:
I think the pixel gameplay is very attractive. But the UI is very cartoony and generic AI. The character portraits are okay. They're definitely much better than so much of the Chatgpt AI art that reeks of AI slop. But the food itself is clearly AI generated and does not look appetizing. I would rather have pixel art food that is consistent with the in-game artwork than the AI-generated "higher res" images that something like Chatgpt will give you. It's all quite jarring. The food doesn't match the pixel art or even the character art. So you have a lot of inconsistency in the presentation of the game which makes your game appear like "AI slop" overall. I toyed around with PixelLab and at least that you can match the pixel art style with what you have and I personally find it more appealing than the food you have on display. At the very least, maybe try matching the food art style to the character portraits? Are you using a color palette for the whole game? It feels like the UI is on an entirely different palette from the in-game pixel artwork.

https://preview.redd.it/vq8jpve2frvh1.png?width=855&format=png&auto=webp&s=ddfda87d887bda9e84a298fe9e16c31d1a877153

replies.author: rychder
replies.body: Taking notes from all of this, I think a consistent color palette is a great place to start making improvements. Also I’ll look into Pixel Lab, I initially started with Claude’s defaulted 8bit pixel art which was very muted and unappetizing looking but there’s probably a middle ground between that and what I switched to where it’s pixel style but still decent looking. Thank you for the feedback!
